comment_data.body:
> They are very annoying as i must write something within that field or it would stay there forever until i reopen the file! And when i change a function to another and accepted the suggestion a circle would be placed before the semicolon forcing me to write another semicolon while there is a one!

They come from 'mini.snippets' and show empty tabstops that need to be visited in order to finish the snippet session. There are several ways to act here:
- Actually fill tabstops and finish snippet session. You can read more about it [here](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-snippets.html#minisnippets.default_insert-sessionlifecycle). This is my suggested approach, since those completion candidates are marked as snippets for a reason.
- Adjust how snippet is inserted to not show empty tabstops by using [`empty_tabstop` and `empty_tabstop_final`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-snippets.html#minisnippets.default_insert-parameters) options. There is an example [here](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-snippets.html#minisnippets.config-expand). See how `config.expand.insert` is customized. Set to empty string to hide it. But I would not recommend it, since there would still be loose snippet sessions and that might be problematic.
